quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic moving in opposite directions, what should you do?

options.text: Move back to your lane when you have enough space between you and the car you passed.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Move back to the right side of the road right away.
Drive in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move back to your lane when you have enough space between you and the car you passed.
questions.explanation: When passing on a two-lane road, return to the right side of the road once you have enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.

questions.question: When it starts to rain while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Drive faster than the other cars.
Drive at the highest posted speed limit.
Slow down.
Follow the car in front of you closely.

questions.explanation: When heavy rain makes it hard to see, reduce your speed. Turn on your headlights so other drivers can see you. If rain is so heavy that you cannot see well, pull to the side of the road and stop until it clears.

questions.question: What can you do to prevent hydroplaning?

options.text: Make sure your tires have good tread.
Keep your tires filled to the right pressure.
Slow down when driving in the rain.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, keep your tires in good condition with deep tread, keep them filled to the correct pressure, and drive slower in the rain. Hydroplaning happens most often at high speeds.

questions.question: The driver in front of you stops at a crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Carefully pass the car at 10 mph or slower.
Stop and only go when all pedestrians have crossed.
Change lanes, look, and pass the stopped car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and only go when all pedestrians have crossed.
questions.explanation: Do not pass a stopped car at a crosswalk. There may be pedestrians you cannot see. Stop and wait until all pedestrians have finished crossing.

questions.question: As you enter a roundabout, you should slow down and:

options.text: Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing.
Yield to cars already in the roundabout.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and all traffic already inside the roundabout.

questions.question: Drivers do not have to let pedestrians cross in a marked crosswalk.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Drivers must stop completely and let pedestrians cross in marked crosswalks. Drivers must also yield to pedestrians in unmarked crosswalks on the driver's side when there are no traffic signals.

questions.question: As blood alcohol concentration (BAC) increases, you become:

options.text: More intoxicated.
More sober.
More coordinated.

questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in your blood. The higher your BAC, the more impaired you become.

questions.question: A driver who goes much slower than the speed limit:

options.text: Is always a very safe driver.
Always has the right-of-way.
Should not let cars behind them pass.
May create a dangerous driving situation.

questions.correctAnswerText: May create a dangerous driving situation.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic can be unsafe. On a two-lane road, if you drive so slowly that cars are backing up behind you, you must pull off the road to let them pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when conditions require it.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Reduce your speed when the road is wet.
The road ahead has a series of turns or curves.
More traffic is coming.
A steep hill is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed when the road is wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road is slippery when wet. In wet conditions, slow down, avoid sudden braking or turning, and increase your distance from the car ahead.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Pedestrians walking along the road nearby.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
Pedestrians must not cross here.

questions.explanation: This yellow and black warning sign tells drivers that pedestrians may be crossing ahead. If a pedestrian is crossing in a marked crosswalk, drivers must stop and stay stopped until the pedestrian leaves the crosswalk.

questions.question: How can you help the driver behind you stay a safe distance away?

options.text: Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.
Drive 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
Keep a steady speed.

questions.explanation: Keep a steady speed and signal before turning, changing lanes, or slowing down. This helps the driver behind you stay a safe distance away.

questions.question: When driving near children playing, what should you expect?

options.text: They will know when it is safe to cross the street.
They will stop at the curb before crossing.
They will run into the street without looking.
They will not cross unless with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: They will run into the street without looking.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be very careful when children are nearby. Children may run into the street suddenly without looking first.

questions.question: When passing a car that just parked on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Expect the driver to open the door as you approach.
Speed up.
Brake hard.
Expect the driver to wait for you to pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the driver to open the door as you approach.
questions.explanation: When passing a parked car, expect the driver to open the door as you go by. Drive carefully and stay alert around parked vehicles.

questions.question: You should leave extra space in front of your car when following a:

options.text: Station wagon.
Passenger car.
Motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Leave extra space behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop faster than other vehicles. You also need room to stop if the motorcycle brakes or the rider falls. Motorcycles are hard to see at night because they have only one tail light.

questions.question: Talking or texting on a cell phone while driving will not greatly increase your chance of a crash.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.explanation: Using a phone while driving is a distraction that increases your risk of crashing.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Look through the rear window.
Press hard on the gas pedal.
Use only your rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: Put your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look directly out the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors because they do not show what is directly behind your car. Back up slowly.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light means you should:

options.text: Slow down and proceed carefully.
Stop as quickly as possible.
Stop and go only when the intersection is clear.

questions.explanation: At a flashing yellow light, slow down and proceed with caution. You do not need to stop.

questions.question: At an intersection with a flashing yellow light, you must:

options.text: Wait for a green light before going.
Slow down and cross carefully.
Stop before crossing.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be aware. Proceed with caution. Watch for other traffic and pedestrians crossing.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Crossroad ahead.
Merge.
Stop.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that a crossroad is ahead.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, you should:

options.text: Pump the brake pedal quickly several times.
Slow down gradually without braking.
Press the brake pedal hard.

questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the car straight. Take your foot off the gas and do not brake. Let the car slow down on its own. Use the brakes gently only if needed. Pull over when safe.

questions.question: You must obey instructions from school crossing guards:

options.text: At all times.
Only during school hours.
Unless you do not see any children present.

questions.explanation: Always obey crossing guards near schools. Watch for them and follow their instructions.

questions.question: When driving near heavy trucks, you must allow extra space for:

options.text: The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.
The decreased stopping distance required by large vehicles.
The decreased noise of larger vehicles.
The increased speed of larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.
questions.explanation: Heavy trucks need more distance to stop. Stay where the truck driver can see you. Do not block their view of the road.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with a crossbuck sign but no gates or flashing lights, you should:

options.text: Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you know no train is coming.
Turn your radio down to listen for an approaching train.
Only continue when a flagger clears you to do so, if applicable.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always approach railroad crossings with extreme caution. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. Lower your radio volume to listen for trains. Follow any flagger's instructions.

questions.question: Which of these must you obey first?

options.text: A steady red light
A police officer
A stop sign
A flashing red light

questions.explanation: A police officer's directions take priority over all signs, signals, and road markings.

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, you should:

options.text: Do not proceed until the children wave to you.
Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
Accelerate quickly.
Turn on your emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After the school bus stops, watch for children walking near the road. Drive carefully around children.
